policies.n: Second-group ordinary passports do not receive a nationality-only waiver. The 14-day nonextendable waiver requires residence or a valid entry visa for the United States, Canada, Australia, United Kingdom, a Schengen country or Japan; alternatively GCC residence and a profession eligible for the resident-visa facility. Passport must be valid at least six months; return ticket, confirmed hotel, health insurance and sufficient funds required. Husband/wife/children may benefit under the accompanying-family provision even with another nationality. No qualifying foreign status or family eligibility is assumed. Without a qualifying waiver, obtain the appropriate ROP visa/entry permission; the source does not establish a uniform visa product or its stay length for this group.
policies.label: Visa required unless conditional 14-day waiver applies
policies.stay: Conditional waiver: 14 days; otherwise as authorized by the applicable visa

policies.n: Ordinary passport holders under 15 or above 50 are visa-exempt for tourist visits up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Holders aged 15–50 require a visa. The MFA offers a one-month single-entry eVisa at ages 15–18 or 35–50 when holding a valid Schengen-member, US, UK or Irish visa or residence permit, subject to the additional eVisa conditions. Neither age nor foreign-document eligibility is assumed. For a required visa, authorized stay follows the issued product; the one-month eVisa period is not assigned to all visa methods.
policies.label: Age-dependent waiver or visa requirement
policies.stay: Qualifying age waiver: 90 days in any 180 days; visa branch: as issued

policies.n: Ordinary Egyptian passports require a visa. Applicants under 15 or above 45 may obtain an eVisa without the additional foreign-document condition. Ages 15–45 may obtain the stated 30-day single-entry eVisa only with a valid Schengen, US, UK or Irish visa/residence permit and travel on Turkish Airlines, AJet, Pegasus, Egypt Air or Air Cairo. No age or qualifying foreign document is assumed. A uniform stay for the other visa branches is not stated.
policies.label: Visa required; eVisa eligibility depends on age/documents
policies.stay: Conditional age-15–45 eVisa: 30 days; other visa branches: stay not established

policies.n: MFA explicitly requires visas for ordinary Taiwan passports and offers a single-entry eVisa described as valid for one month subject to certain conditions. Those additional conditions were not fully established, so this records the visa requirement with electronic-method uncertainty, not a finding that eVisa is unavailable. The visa-validity period is not encoded as a confirmed stay.
policies.label: Visa required; conditional eVisa channel

policies.n: Ordinary short-tourist entry requires a visa under Resolution 5488 Articles 2 and 7, after reconciling its Article 3 list and Article 6 treaty exception against the current public treaty register. Diplomatic/service-only and visa-fee waivers do not exempt ordinary passports. No qualifying third-country permanent residence under the Pacific Alliance/Andean provisions is assumed. The MFA states the process is 100% virtual and the approved visa is emailed; apply to the office competent for the actual residence. Tourist visa permits 90 days initially, extendable by another 90 subject to approval; total cannot exceed 180 continuous or discontinuous days within 365 days from visa issue. Up-to-one-year visa validity is not a one-year stay.

Valid ordinary Mongolian passport; treaty effective 26 January 2026, confirmed in force by the MFA registry. Up to 90 days in any 180-day period from first entry, through authorized international border crossings. Tourism covered; remunerated activities require the appropriate visa. Any extension is subject to national law, not automatic.

Valid Belarus citizen passport expressly included in Annex 1.1. Treaty entered into force 19 December 2025 according to the MFA register. Article 1 says 90 days within a calendar year from the date of first entry; preserve that wording rather than substituting a 90/180 rule or a new allowance per visit. Use authorized international passenger crossings. Longer uninterrupted stays require a visa; exceptional extensions are individually authorized.
policies.stay: 90 days within a calendar year from the date of first entry (treaty wording)

policies.n: Advance electronic visa authorization is required before travel under the regime effective 5 January 2025. Obtain the electronic approval through ANRPTS; border biometric/payment/issuance formalities are subsequent steps, not a separate walk-up visa-on-arrival option. Use an authorized international crossing. The source does not establish a single unconditional tourist stay applicable to all approved products, so stay follows the authorization. This evidence is limited to this origin nationality.
policies.label: Advance eVisa authorization required

policies.n: Palestinian ordinary passports have an expressly documented Chinese visa process: the Representative Office fee schedule names Palestinian passports and its instructions include tourist L visas. Apply online for preliminary review, then deliver the original passport and any required biometrics to the office and collect the issued passport/visa. This is not an end-to-end eVisa. Passport valid at least six months with blank visa pages; itinerary/accommodation or qualifying invitation required. Visa officer determines validity, stay and entries; none is inferred from processing days or fee bands. Stateless or other-country-issued Palestinian travel documents are not automatically covered.
policies.label: Tourist visa; Palestinian passport process established

policies.n: Belgian Embassy Nairobi expressly accepts Somali short-stay C-visa applications within its stated citizenship/residence jurisdiction, in person through TLS. The baseline EU recognition matrix does not recognize ordinary Somali passports in Belgium: a visa/document authorization must therefore use the applicable limited-territorial/separate-sheet mechanism under Visa Code Articles 25(3) and 29(2), rather than assuming that any Schengen visa validates the passport. Confirm the issued Belgian authorization and transit itinerary; no permission for other Schengen states is assumed. The mission states standard processing of 45 days and no multiple-entry visas; 45 days is not a stay grant. Permitted stay follows the issued permission and admission remains an individual decision.
policies.label: Visa and document-specific authorization required

findings: Added only German and Serbian ordinary-passport requirements from actual origin-government content. UAE checker was inspected and rejected for resolution: it says Visa Free for normal passports but then says ordinary passports obtain arrival/embassy visas with incompatible fee figures.

Fresh CEMAC Commission interview of 8 September 2025 expressly confirms visa-free regional circulation is effective, unlike the old UDEAC scan. It does not supply the currently accepted ordinary/biometric passport schedule, national exceptions or stay grant; CM/CG/GA/GQ/TD remain unresolved at that document-specific level. No unrestricted fm category inferred.
All other assigned origins still lack an exhaustive current ordinary-passport exemption/default schedule. Failed US official retrievals are not evidence of an entry ban.

Added FR/DE/BE/ES advance eVisa requirements using explicit nationality-specific official advice. Signed Ministry Circular 66 of 3 January 2025 visually inspected: it directs visa requests to ANRPTS, without an exhaustive nationality rule.

Reviewed the prior French/Arabic agreement lists and fresh Ministry Conventions page. The latter is a human-rights/governance/terrorism treaty index, not an inbound visa schedule. Diplomatic-only waivers, outbound Mauritanian concessions and fee bands do not settle other ordinary passports.
ANRPTS French entry point fails TLS EOF. Remaining origins need a current exhaustive inbound exemption/default or actual nationality decision; no blanket eVisa mandate from an application form.

Added CA/DE/FR/RS visa requirements with explicit electronic-method uncertainty. The Paris consulate page now expressly enumerates the 12 current ECOWAS countries and requires valid ECOWAS travel documentation for that exemption; existing ECOWAS baseline routes are not recounted.

Presidency material on the AES biometric passport and 2025 adoption was inspected, together with prior 14 December 2024 confederal declaration. These do not conclusively supply the BF/NE ordinary-passport and legacy-document branches into Mali. No visa waiver inferred from opposite-direction ECOWAS concessions, fees or reciprocity.

Other origins lack current exhaustive ordinary exemptions and nationality-specific electronic processing. US restriction reports were not promoted without accessible operative primary content; current source-specific Serbian/consular limitations are preserved.

All 24 named second-group gaps resolved as conditional rules using current English and Arabic Foreign Ministry regulations. No foreign visa/residence, profession, accompanying-family eligibility or age is assumed.

The other 90 origins remain unresolved: ROP page retrieved is a work/family/student visa page rather than tourist eligibility; the Ministry directs these applicants to product-specific assessment. No uniform sponsored/eVisa product or blanket nationality refusal inferred.

Reconciled the express statutory visa default with the live public treaty registry: active visa-name and Visa-topic queries plus Migration/Tourism topics inspected. Signed Mongolia and Belarus treaty texts and actual in-force metadata recovered; their durations differ.

84 ordinary-nationality gaps have electronic tourist-visa requirements after Articles 3–6 reconciliation; two treaty waivers are separately recorded. Pacific Alliance/Andean residence exceptions are not assumed. The registry test row PRUEBA is not a legal instrument or an entry-rule source.

MO/PS/XK remain unresolved for ordinary-document recognition/territorial treatment. A diplomatic Palestinian treaty and an application country label do not independently settle every ordinary travel document. No blanket negative rule assigned to these three.

Fresh MOFA consular page, MOI public visa-services page and Hayya tourist page inspected. MOFA expressly handles cases that cannot be applied for electronically but supplies no nationality-specific decisions for CV/IL/KI/XK/MH/FM/NR.

Hayya retrieval exposes a nationality question and generic GCC text, not a completed result for these seven. Existing Visit Qatar selector omissions are not interpreted as refusal, automatic eVisa entitlement or exemption. All seven remain unresolved.
All five gaps resolved: DZ/IQ/LY age-conditioned waivers versus visas; EG age/document/airline-conditioned electronic eligibility; TW explicit requirement with unverified additional eVisa conditions.
No uniform 90-day or one-month stay assigned across distinct age/method branches. Electronic eligibility uncertainty does not erase an explicit visa requirement.

Fresh Ministry treaty announcements found for Ghana and UAE, and UAE mission-opening text. Ghana announcement proves signature but provides no operative passport scope, commencement or stay; UAE 2016 announcement includes ordinary passports and projected commencement but does not establish supersession of the contradictory live Immigration lists.

BA/GH/AE remain conflicted. SS remains absent from visa schedules; its presence in the tourism yellow-fever list is a vaccination rule, not visa evidence. No article, dropdown or fee treated as an operative exemption.

Fresh state-broadcaster searches for Macao and Sudan visa amendments found no operative ordinary-passport replacement rule. Reviewed preserved signed 002-2026 pages 13–14: notification and commencement clauses, not an omitted-country default.

XK/MO/SS remain omitted from the actual 2026 schedule. Legislature request timed out; apparent consuladodenicaragua.com content is unrelated/old news and was rejected as current consular evidence. No substitute nationality selected.

PS resolved through source-language Representative Office instructions plus an explicit Palestinian-passport visa-fee table, combined with the baseline statutory requirement. Online application followed by original-passport submission is vr, not ev.

XK remains unresolved: attempted Serbian mission consular route redirects to homepage and supplies no Kosovo ordinary-passport or substitute-document determination. No non-recognition-based blanket ban.

SO resolved as a qualified visa/document-authorization route: actual mission page expressly covers Somali short-stay applicants; EU law provides territorial/separate-sheet mechanism. Existing non-recognition finding remains, rather than being replaced by ordinary Schengen-passport acceptance.
The 45-day processing period and single-entry restriction are explicit; neither is a tourist stay allowance.

Fresh Norwegian police homepage/search and Russian-language mission guidance inspected. The mission still explicitly refers the restrictions effective 29 May 2024 to UDI; generic tourist-application text does not override those restrictions.

Government English/native announcements, UDI and the UDI legal-guidance site return 403; no bypass. RU remains unresolved for the controlling border/territorial/exception rule, not simply classified vr or a nationality-wide ban.
Fresh Interior admission-schedule page retrieved, but no Kosovo ordinary-document determination found. Travel-document/service/search alternatives return 404.
XK remains unresolved: the ordinary-state residual visa rule does not by itself establish Kosovo passport acceptance. No non-recognition-only entry ban inferred.
